Peanut Butter Is a Bamboo-Filled Camper Van With a Cozy Interior Built for Off-Grid Adventures
49 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans
Bamboo is a really popular material for camper van conversions. However, it's rare to see a conversion that has as much bamboo as the project I'd like to share with you folks today – meet Peanut Butter.
What we have here is a build based on a 2022 4x4 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 144" wheelbase. It was created by Levity Vans, a Santa Cruz, California-based company that specializes in transforming cargo vans into high-end adventure machines.
As always, let's start the tour by taking a look at the exterior. The van's exterior is quite telling, not hiding the fact that this is a camper van – it doesn't "scream" camper van either, as it doesn't have a myriad of upgrades like we see on other projects.
The van rides on black Sprinter wheels wrapped in Kumho Crugen all-season tires. At the rear, you'll come across an Owl Vans spare tire carrier, as well as a bumper step.
On the roof, you'll come across a Fiamma manual awning and a 400 W solar array. Other notable exterior mods are side steps, Rolef bug screens, and a set of flares.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are super common on Sprinters because this model is narrower compared to other popular camper base vehicles, like the Ram ProMaster or the Ford Transit.
Flares are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south setup. This rig's Vanspeed capsules have been color matched to the van's paint and come with half-slider windows.
Stepping inside, you'll immediately feel the warm embrace of the bamboo design. Of course, making the entire interior with bamboo would've probably been an eye-sore. In this van, all the cabinetry was made out of bamboo plywood, as well as some other elements, such as a headliner shelf.
The rest of the design consists of walls upholstered in light grey fabric, a soft tan ceiling, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring. The look is complemented by some stainless steel elements, like the cabinet and drawer handles or the sink faucet, as well as a black solid surface countertop.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans A key detail is that the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. This layout is a must on small-wheelbase vans like this Sprinter, as it helps make the living space feel roomier.
The driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van and used after you've set up camp.
This front seating area continues further back in the form of a Bellagio bench seat offering room for two people. It comes with seatbelts and armrests, but the best part about it is that it can be folded flat and raised out of the way, to the side. Moreover, the seating area is completed by a large Lagun table mount that can be easily removed. By the way, the elements in this space were added after the video tour and photos of the van were taken.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units, one on each side of the living space. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cutting board insert and a separate filtered water faucet, a microwave oven, a large Isotherm Cruise 130 12V fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, and a single-burner induction stovetop.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans A flip-up table extends the standard 36 inches (91 centimeters) of meal prep area to a total of 55 inches (139 centimeters). Moreover, a Maxxair vent fan is perfectly positioned above the induction stove to draw out the smells and fumes from cooking.
Three overhead cabinets, four drawers with soft-close mechanisms, and two lower cabinets are available for storage. One of the lower cabinets houses a composting toilet and has two flip-up panels that can double as steps to get into bed.
Finally, the rear part of the living space is taken up by a fixed bed arrangement that's 79.5 inches (202 centimeters) long and 60 inches (152 centimeters) wide. You'll also notice two overhead cabinets, charging points (both USB and standard outlets), and two reading lights with a red function that's ideal to use at night.
The bed platform is positioned quite high up, making room for a large garage underneath. It offers abundant space in the middle, while its sides are taken up by two tall boxes – they integrate storage compartments and accommodate the utility systems. The bed platform and the two boxes are also made out of bamboo ply.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans To make loading and unloading items in the garage easier, the builders fitted a pull-out tray. It's attached to heavy-duty slides that can support up to 500 lb. (227 kg) and has an L-Track that allows you to secure gear or large items. The garage is definitely tall enough to accommodate a mountain bike, provided you remove the front wheel.
Power is on the left side - the electrical system's highlights are a 300 Ah BattleBorn battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. Furthermore, you can use solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging to keep the batteries topped off – if used correctly and cleverly, it's possible to never run out of juice.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 27-gallon (102-liter) freshwater tank, an 11-gallon (41-liter) greywater tank, and an outdoor shower connection with a pull-out sprayer. Both water tanks are mounted underneath the vehicle, and the greywater one can be dumped at the flip of a switch thanks to an electronic dump valve.
The last important system in this rig is a Rixen's hydronic heater that provides both heated air and hot water.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans The "command center" for the rig's utilities is integrated onto the side of one of the kitchen overhead cabinets, conveniently located by the entrance. It includes four dimmer light switches, a battery monitor, an inverter controller, a thermostat for the Rixen's heating system, and switches for a garage light and a water pump.
All in all, the Peanut Butter build by Levity Vans has the right blend of fine aesthetics and home-like functionality.
When I started researching this camper van, I was bummed to discover that Levity Vans is no longer in business. I say bummed because it's sad to see that companies who create awesome homes on wheels go out of business due to financial reasons.
Levity Vans operated for a total of 9 years, but it was not able to continue operations due to the changing market and various financial pressures. Still, I feel like its creations deserve some attention. Stay tuned, as I'll be taking a look at other of its builds here on autoevolution.
